successCriteria.description: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md contains exactly ONE occurrence of the heading "### Phase 7 delivered (web approvals queue consumes GET /leaves/pending-decisions)" (it currently contains two, at lines 1760 and 1772).

The surviving "Phase 7 delivered (web approvals queue consumes GET /leaves/pending-decisions)" block is byte-identical to the removed duplicate (pure de-duplication, no content loss), and the "Stale text left in place" bullet appears exactly once in the file.

Business rule 2 in the "Feature: Notify the approver when a leave request is cancelled" section no longer asserts an unconditional approver-notification count: it states the approver notification is emitted only when the resolved approver is not the cancelling actor, and that when the actor IS the resolved approver zero approver notifications are written.

Rule 2 is consistent with rule 5 (recipient set = requester + resolved approver, actor removed, duplicates collapsed, at most two, may be empty) and rule 9 (self-notification suppressed) in the same section: no rule in the section states a notification count that contradicts another rule in the section.

The corrected rule 2 matches the built behaviour and the pinned test: src/modules/leave/leave.service.ts cancellationRecipients drops any notice whose recipientId === actor.id, and tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.service.test.ts "notifies only the requester when the manager who approved it cancels it" asserts exactly one notification with recipientId === REQUESTER_ID.

No other section of docs/ARCHITECTURE.md is altered: the "Phase 1 delivered (notifications.related_entity_code migration)" block, the Domain entities / Lifecycle states / Conceptual tables / Repository interfaces / Module boundaries / Dependency map / Cross-cutting contracts / Recommended phases / Open questions / Stack compliance subsections of the cancellation feature, and every other feature section are unchanged.

constraints: Documentation-only phase: the ONLY file that may change is docs/ARCHITECTURE.md. No file under src/, web/src/, tests/, migrations/, or scripts/ may be modified, and no new file may be created.

The built code is the source of truth for the corrected rule 2, not the reverse: the fix must NOT change src/modules/leave/leave.service.ts (cancellationRecipients / resolveApproverRecipient) or tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.service.test.ts to match the stale prose.

The corrected rule 2 must cite the same authority the rest of the section already cites — CLARIFY-006 in docs/DECISIONS.md, amended 2026-10-09 ("Every recipient is notified EXCEPT the actor who performed the cancellation") — and must not introduce a new decision, ADR, or CLARIFY number.

The de-duplication must remove exactly one of the two byte-identical "Phase 7 delivered (web approvals queue consumes GET /leaves/pending-decisions)" blocks (lines 1760-1771 and 1772-1783) and keep the other verbatim; the block's content must not be rewritten, merged, or reworded while removing it.

The corrected rule 2 must keep the parts of the rule that are still true and load-bearing: the notification is not duplicated per approver candidate, is not sent to both the recorded approver and the current manager, and is not re-sent on a retry (a repeat cancel fails its state guard and emits nothing).

The corrected rule 2 must not contradict the section's own "Lifecycle states" named transitions (cancelInPlace / reverseApproved both "emit the approver notification") or the "Transaction" contract (the approver notification insert is step (d) of the single unit of work) — those statements describe the emission path, not the recipient count, and must remain true as written.
The edit must not touch the "Stale text left in place" bullet's substance (the web-approvals dependency-map line is still stale) — only the duplicate copy of it is removed.
outOfScope: Fixing the stale "Dependency map" line that still lists web-infrastructure-api as a web-approvals dependency (the "Stale text left in place" bullet documents it deliberately; correcting the map itself is a separate change).

Reconciling the other documented-vs-built drifts in the same feature section (e.g. the leave_requests status/approver_id indexes and the reverses_request_id IS NOT NULL queue predicate described in "Conceptual tables" and "Repository interfaces" but not built) — only the two review findings are in scope.
Any change to the "Open questions" subsection of the cancellation feature, including removing the now-settled "self-notification suppression" item from that list.
Editing docs/DECISIONS.md (CLARIFY-006 and ADR-002..ADR-005 are already correct and are the authority the corrected rule cites).
Adding, changing, or re-running any test; the phase is documentation-only and the existing pinned tests already encode the correct behaviour.

entityInvariants.invariant: A cancellation writes one Notification row per recipient in the set {requester, resolved approver} minus the cancelling actor, de-duplicated by recipient id; the set holds at most two recipients and may be empty, and an empty set notifies nobody while the cancellation still succeeds. The approver notification is emitted only when the resolved approver is not the cancelling actor.

Created PENDING inside the same unit of work as the status change, keyed to the ORIGINAL request id (never the GP-008 reversal row's id), carrying relatedEntityType 'leave_request', relatedEntityCode = the request's canonical lowercase leaveTypeCode, and the existing type literal 'leave_request'; it is never advanced to SENT by the cancellation.

Exactly one CANCEL entry per cancellation, with unchanged shape: action AuditAction.CANCEL, entityType LEAVE_REQUEST_ENTITY_TYPE, entityId = the ORIGINAL request id, beforeState/afterState present; a skipped approver notification is recorded as a boolean approverNotificationSkipped key merged into afterState, never as a new field or nested object.
